observations: Two isolated, constant-width material paths run left-to-right and never merge.
The paths begin and end widely separated, approach one another smoothly near the horizontal midpoint, and separate symmetrically.
The local material thickness is approximately 0.65 um throughout, so the apparent widening in sloped regions is raster projection rather than a taper.
The center-to-center separation changes from approximately 2.34 um at the facets to approximately 0.95 um at the closest approach, giving an edge gap near 0.30 um.
topology_reasoning.operation: The smoothly varying separation brings the guides into an evanescent-coupling regime around the center. Optical power transfers through supermode beating while the gradual approach and departure suppress abrupt transition loss.
topology_reasoning.modeling_plan: Construct both centerlines as mirrored sampled gf.Path objects with smooth raised-cosine approach/departure sections and a tunable central transfer section, then extrude on layer (1,0). Keep delta_length at zero in the recreation; it is a real one-arm extension knob retained to satisfy the independent geometry-response contract.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitives-only construction: two mirrored smootherstep gf.Path centerlines, 0.65 um extrusion width, 0.31 um coupling gap, 0.695 um approach offset, and zero-length central plateau. The residual is a thin, symmetric boundary mismatch from the analytic curve shape; the result exceeds the 0.85 stop threshold, so no further image-fitting iteration was performed.
